beats.say: In nineteen thirty-six, five hundred and fifty-eight Sikh officers served in Shanghai's police.
Why were men from Punjab policing Chinese streets?
Hong Kong, under British rule, did it first.
In eighteen sixty-two, its police chief found his Bombay recruits disappointing.
So he hired Sikhs straight from Punjab, and they did better.
They wore turbans, not caps, earning the nickname "big heads".
In eighteen eighty-four, amid France–China tensions, Shanghai's International Settlement hired sixteen Sikh constables.
By late eighteen eighty-five there were fifty, some recruited from Lahore.
By nineteen thirty-six, sixteen had become five hundred and fifty-eight.
